proposal.name: Exact Go acceptance with independent evidence

issue_plan.name: Exact Go acceptance with independent evidence
issue_plan.summary: Deliver issue #523 in three reviewable pull requests: safe Go command selection and package discovery, independent runtime completion evidence, then attributable proposed-API compiler failures and complete lifecycle verification. Together they provide a working Go adapter through the existing lower-level configured lifecycle, using captured commands and verified offline environments while preserving pinned identities, source bytes and shared budgets. Configured factory admission, external plumbing and the other native framework adapters remain disabled, and the built-in Go runner and legacy hashes and locks remain compatible. Each issue updates SPEC.md and docs/factory.md for its implemented behavior and keeps README.md accurate within 400 lines; the merger records the new adapter execution decision before the following integration issue.

issues.title: Resolve exact Go acceptance selections under captured commands
issues.body:
Implement the selection and discovery portion of #523, the Go adapter step of #513 within #452's ratified plan. The existing #515 lifecycle in internal/plumbing/repository_acceptance.go and repository_checks.go validates pinned native plans, stages sources privately, prepares captured dependencies and delegates individual evidence to a trusted environment. Add production Go selection and toolchain discovery APIs that this lifecycle can use; their results establish which test may run, not that a test completed. This pull request must be independently usable and tested for selection and discovery without depending on the later runtime collector.

Implement a host-selected Go RepositoryAcceptanceAdapter for each owning part's captured test_one command. Validate all invocation forms before dependency preparation or workload execution. Support safe direct go test argument arrays with exactly one {test} placeholder as the value of -run or -run=, accepting both {test} and ^{test}$ forms. In particular, support ["go", "test", "./...", "-run", "^{test}$", "-count=1"]. Narrow that scope to the actual package containing the acceptance file relative to the owning part, retaining its ordinary production sources and dependencies. Do not run go test on the acceptance source alone. Escape each literal slash-separated selector component with Go regexp rules and anchor each component separately, including every level of an exact subtest path. Prefixes, regexp punctuation, shell syntax, glob characters and option-looking components remain literal data.

Keep applicable build tags and every supported declared execution policy. Validate package scope rather than silently overriding an explicit scope which excludes the target; refuse forms whose inclusion or narrowing cannot be established safely. Reject conflicting or repeated selection flags, repetitions and modes that cannot produce one fresh completed selection, opaque executables or wrappers, unsupported arguments, and unsafe command forms with explicit reasons. Never substitute a different command policy, fall back to the built-in runner, or interpolate selector data into shell or interpreter source, including sh -c equivalents. Any trusted process wrapper may pass arguments positionally only. The documentation must state the actual supported forms and refusal reasons rather than claim arbitrary go test compatibility.

After safe command validation and private staging, discover the package through the prepared Go toolchain under the same build constraints and execution policy that will test it. Establish that the requested top-level function is a valid Go testing declaration in the pinned acceptance file, that the toolchain actually includes that file, and that exactly one declaration is selected. Handle both ordinary and external test packages. Distinguish identical function names in other files, packages, modules and parts; refuse wrong-file declarations, files excluded by tags or filename/platform constraints, duplicates and multiple matches. A path-derived package hint alone is not discovery authority. Discovery may identify the top-level function of a subtest selector but must not claim the subtest exists or completed; runtime confirmation is the next issue.

Provide a production discovery path that works inside the prepared pinned Go environment and can also be exercised with real local Go processes in default tests. Preserve the common source and execution binding, deepest-part ownership and verbatim source staging. The discovery API must accept the inherited bounded context, return structured refusal/setup information, and leave no selection or completion claim on missing Go/compiler tools, unresolved dependencies, invalid module/package discovery or interruption. Command-form validation consumes the original whole-run allowance; acceptance discovery and compilation consume the shared test-phase allowance once that phase begins. Never reset either budget, enable network or installation, download tools or dependencies, require Python, or rely on a host Go cache.

Default Go tests must use small standard-library-only temporary modules and the production selection/discovery code, with real Go discovery and compilation where needed and isolated writable caches. Cover both -run spellings and placeholder forms, the documented ./... command, a nested package, applicable build tags, ordinary and external tests, identical names across packages/modules/parts, wrong-file and excluded-file refusals, duplicate declarations and multiple matches. Verify exact component patterns with regexp punctuation, prefix neighbors, glob and shell-looking text and option-looking subtest data. Exercise scope exclusion, unsafe and conflicting command forms, missing tool, unresolved dependency, discovery failure and canceled discovery; assert unsupported templates reach neither preparation nor execution. Inspect actual argument boundaries, working directories and offline environment requests so fake subprocess output cannot stand in for package discovery.

Inspect internal/plumbing/native.go and native_identity_accept_test.go, acceptance_lifecycle_accept_test.go, acceptance_foundation_regression_test.go, acceptance_budget_accept_test.go, repository_sandbox_accept_test.go and repository_container_accept_test.go before planning. Their fakes pin command arguments, selection, budgets and isolation. Name existing tests needing changes in the file-level plan and preserve pinned kept behavior.

Keep all defaults and factory admission unchanged. Selection/discovery alone cannot make configured planning proposable or a native build ready. The production runtime evidence collector and compiler-failure qualification are subsequent issues in this ordered plan; until then these helpers supply no completed acceptance evidence. Candidate-controlled adapter registration is forbidden, pytest/Vitest/Jest remain unsupported, and external plumbing stays disabled. Preserve the unconfigured Go runner, legacy hashes and locks without metadata inference or migration.

Update SPEC.md and docs/factory.md in this change to describe the available selection/discovery API, supported captured commands and remaining runtime restriction. Keep README.md accurate and at most 400 lines, with details in its linked factory page. Cite existing decisions in every changed SPEC bullet. Foundations: D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301 and D-0305; #484/D-0311's captured execution API; #503/D-0314's native identity contract; and #515/D-0316's shared lifecycle. The build cannot write decisions/: the merger records the new selection/execution decision before the next issue. Decision recording and checks blocked by unavailable Docker/network are Merger work, while affected real Python and TLAPS suites remain required in CI.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Collect independent Go runtime completion through the shared lifecycle
issues.body:
Implement #523's production Go runtime adapter after the preceding exact-selection and toolchain-discovery issue has merged. This is the second issue of the ordered #523 plan, continuing #513 within #452. Reuse those production selection/discovery APIs and #515's RepositoryChecks.Adapters, RepositoryAcceptanceEnvironment.RunAcceptance, fresh invocation bindings, private source staging and evidence validation. Deliver a working lower-level path through Sandbox.checkRepositoryBase and explicitly configured Sandbox.Run for real Go assertion failures and candidate successes, including the prepared Docker environment; do not connect factory planning admission or default adapter registration.

Execute each acceptance selector separately, in its owning part's directory, through its captured and safely narrowed test_one command. Preserve the command policy validated by the preceding issue, normal production files and dependencies, build constraints and exact literal component selection. The full (part, framework, file, selector) identity and source bytes remain pinned and bound to the captured execution digest. Perform real package/declaration discovery before treating execution as the selected test. Keep unsupported forms refused before preparation/execution. The environment must support a trusted evidence transport independent of workload stdout and stderr, without requiring Python, a host Go cache, installation, downloads or network in the pinned Go image.

Collect actual Go testing start and terminal lifecycle evidence, retaining enough parent/child lifecycle to verify the requested exact subtest. Bind it to the host's fresh invocation ID, complete identity, discovered package, source digest and execution digest. Require exactly one matching completed selection; running only a parent, sibling or parameterized family cannot satisfy a requested exact child. A process exit, textual PASS/FAIL, test2json-looking JSON, synthetic process-exit failure or a fabricated runner marker is never sufficient. Both stdout and stderr, before and during tests, remain diagnostics even when they contain plausible or framed lifecycle data. Do not obtain apparent independence merely by parsing those diagnostics into a new record format.

A completed assertion failure or panic with authentic framework failure completion qualifies as test/failed. A selected skip is explicitly test/skipped and qualifies as neither a pass nor a base failure. Zero-test success, an absent selector, TestMain exiting before m.Run, a nonzero abrupt exit, an interrupted process or a missing terminal event cannot qualify. Reject duplicate, stale, contradictory, truncated or mismatched evidence, including results from another file, package, module or part. Preserve relevant running/refused/unstarted statuses and explanatory reasons rather than converting an unattributed exit into failed test evidence. Keep all completed earlier results when later work fails, and preserve full identities and reasons through output clipping and JSON transport.

Run through the shared lifecycle so base checks attempt independent selectors after ordinary suite/test failures and require a completed attributable failure for every acceptance identity; a candidate needs every applicable captured command and each selector to pass. Setup, discovery, transport, exhausted allowances, cancellation and failed cleanup veto qualification. All discovery, compilation, evidence collection and testing consume the inherited twelve-minute whole-run and ten-minute test-phase caps, shortened by caller/preparer limits; the first suite test or acceptance starts the shared phase and neither another selector nor another part resets it. Retain one active disposable part environment, offline verified dependencies, bounded uncanceled cleanup and queue ownership through cleanup.

Default tests must run the production Go selection, discovery and evidence collector with real Go compilation/testing of small standard-library-only modules, without Docker or network. Show a test failing against base production code and passing after only a production change while acceptance bytes remain identical. Show two selected tests in one package where one already passes and the other fails, so the base cannot qualify by broadcasting the failure. Exercise identical names across packages, modules and parts, an external test package, exact nested subtests with regexp punctuation and shell-looking text, prefix/sibling/parameterized neighbors and absent children. Verify that discovery refusals still prevent wrong-file, excluded-file or multiple-match evidence.

Exercise real selected skips, zero-test success, absent selectors, TestMain exit before m.Run, nonzero abrupt exit, genuine assertion failures, panic completion and interruption. Print forged lifecycle lines, test2json JSON and runner records, including framing-looking bytes, to stdout AND stderr before and during execution; they must neither manufacture completion nor override genuine outcomes. Exercise a genuine successful run with fake failure diagnostics as well as incomplete runs with fake success/failure diagnostics. Use the shared lifecycle's environment fault-injection seam to corrupt otherwise real collected evidence for duplicate, stale, conflicting, truncated and wrong-binding records and transport failures; do not use a fake JSON producer instead of Go to test framework outcomes.

Test the production Docker boundary's invocation and transport construction without requiring Docker, preserving its explicit offline environment, pinned prepared image, working directory, argument boundaries, cleanup and lack of host mounts/Python. Keep the core collector identical between those production calls and the local real-Go fixture transport. Add an opt-in prepared-image check if needed for behavior the fake cannot verify; absence of Docker/network is Merger work, not a substitute for the default real-Go tests.

Inspect internal/plumbing/acceptance_lifecycle_accept_test.go, acceptance_evidence_accept_test.go, acceptance_budget_accept_test.go, acceptance_foundation_regression_test.go and acceptance_interruption_regression_test.go; preserve their trusted fake-adapter contracts. Inspect repository_container_accept_test.go, repository_execution_regression_test.go and repository_sandbox_accept_test.go for launch/flag/output assumptions and name existing tests needing modification in the plan. Preserve native_execution_accept_test.go and built-in sandbox coverage.

At this intermediate stage compiler failures without runtime completion remain nonqualifying setup/refusal outcomes; precise proposed-API compiler attribution is the next issue in this plan. A successful compile alone is never a pass. Keep configured factory admission, candidate-controlled registration, external plumbing, pytest, Vitest and Jest disabled. Legacy Go execution, hashes and locks remain compatible without inferred metadata or migration.

Update SPEC.md, docs/factory.md and the README's adapter-status sentence to describe the implemented lower-level Go runtime API, supported forms, independent evidence criteria, compiler restriction and continued factory-admission restriction. README.md stays at most 400 lines; detailed behavior belongs in docs/factory.md. Cite existing decisions in changed SPEC bullets. Foundations: D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301, D-0305, #484/D-0311, #503/D-0314 and #515/D-0316, plus the recorded decision for the preceding selection/discovery issue. The merger records this adapter execution decision before the next issue, since the plumbing build cannot write decisions/. Decision recording and unavailable Docker/network checks are Merger work; affected real Python/TLAPS CI suites remain required.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Attribute proposed-API compiler failures and verify complete Go acceptance
issues.body:
Complete #523's Go adapter after the preceding selection/discovery and runtime-evidence issues have merged. This third and final issue of the ordered plan adds the proposed-new-API base workflow and verifies the complete adapter through the existing lower-level configured lifecycle, closing all remaining #523 work before #513's separate factory integration issue. Reuse captured RepositoryChecks authority, exact native identity and source pinning, verified offline dependencies and the real Go evidence collector; do not enable configured factory admission.

A completed compiler failure may qualify as base evidence only when independently attributed to the selected acceptance package's use of the proposed API. Record that result separately as compile/failed for the fresh invocation and complete identity, with its source and captured execution digests and an explanatory attribution. It is not a runtime start/completion. Establish compiler completion and the relationship to the selected acceptance source/API use through the trusted boundary; arbitrary diagnostics, a nonzero process exit or a failing package/suite alone supply no such authority. Be conservative where attribution is ambiguous.

Do not broadcast one failing compilation to other selectors in the same file, package, module or part. In particular, one acceptance using a missing proposed API cannot supply eligible failure evidence for a neighbor which does not use that API, even when Go compiles them together. Continue using normal package production files and dependencies under the captured command policy; do not substitute a source-only test invocation or rewrite ratified acceptance bytes to make attribution easy. Every independently qualifying compiler result belongs only to its selected invocation. Preserve the existing base requirement that every selector independently fails, and require actual completed passing tests in a fresh candidate run after production implements the API. A successful compile, a suite pass, a cached verdict, a skip or an unstarted selection never qualifies a candidate.

Missing Go/compiler tools, unresolved dependencies, broken package/module discovery, excluded or wrong-file declarations, invalid acceptance source unrelated to the proposed API, unrelated production-source or package failures, interrupted compilation and failed evidence transport are setup/refusal/incomplete outcomes, never eligible base compiler failures. Retain their concrete reasons and distinguish them from attributable compile failures and runtime test failures in structured results and summaries. Preserve earlier completed independent results when a later compiler/setup failure vetoes the run.

Add default Go tests with real compilation and testing of small standard-library-only modules using the production selection, discovery, compiler-attribution and runtime-evidence code. A new-API acceptance must fail on base with attributable compile evidence and then actually pass after only production changes, with identical acceptance bytes. Cover multiple acceptance selectors in one package/file, including a neighbor that already passes and must not inherit the missing-API failure; repeat identities across packages and parts and include an external test package. Exercise missing Go and compiler tools, unresolved dependencies under an offline environment, unrelated package/source failures, broken discovery, syntax failure unrelated to a new API, and interrupted compilation. None may supply eligible evidence. For interruption, synchronize cancellation with actual in-progress compilation via a controlled process/transport seam rather than manufacture compiler result JSON.

Verify the completed adapter end to end through Sandbox.checkRepositoryBase and explicitly host-configured Sandbox.Run. Every base selector must have its own completed test/failed or attributable compile/failed result; applicable candidate commands and every fresh selector must pass. Repeat the production-change-only runtime and proposed-API workflows with unchanged acceptance bytes. Check captured authority against candidate contract changes, altered or linked acceptance files, changed execution binding and stale results. Preserve unsupported-framework and no-adapter refusals before preparation, immutable queue registration, and compatibility with all legacy hashes/locks and the built-in unconfigured Go path.

Exercise budgets across real discovery, compilation, evidence collection and execution, not only a pre-expired context: an earlier selector or suite consumes the allowance available to later selectors and parts, and interruption or exhaustion prevents qualification without losing earlier completed evidence. Keep the shared twelve-minute run and ten-minute test-phase caps, shorter caller/preparer bounds, bounded uncanceled cleanup and queue slot through cleanup. Inspect recorded execution requests for preserved test_one policy, applicable build tags, exact literal package/selector narrowing, offline execution and absence of installation/downloads/Python/host-cache dependencies. Production uses the prepared pinned Go environment; local fixtures use isolated caches and the same production core, without Docker/network.

Retain and run the preceding real-Go runtime cases for skips and absent selectors, zero-test success, TestMain early exit, abrupt exits, assertion/panic completion, exact nested subtests and fabricated stdout/stderr records. Retain the shared-lifecycle corruption cases for duplicate, stale, conflicting, truncated and mismatched evidence and transport failure. These tests and the new compiler cases together must meet the whole #523 contract; do not defer any compiler, selection, evidence, lifecycle or documentation requirement to an unplanned follow-up. The following already-planned #513 integration issue alone owns enabling factory planning, its builder tool and final-check admission.

Inspect the preceding issues' tests and internal/plumbing/acceptance_lifecycle_accept_test.go, acceptance_evidence_accept_test.go, acceptance_budget_accept_test.go, acceptance_interruption_regression_test.go, native_execution_accept_test.go, native_review_regression_test.go, repository_builder_accept_test.go and repository_container_accept_test.go. Name existing tests/fakes needing changes in the plan, including command/flag/output assumptions, and preserve pinned kept behavior. Fault injection tests tool/transport/cancellation boundaries, not Go outcomes.

Update SPEC.md and docs/factory.md to describe the complete implemented Go adapter API, supported safe test_one forms and refusal reasons, independent runtime evidence, attributable compiler failures versus setup failures, and continued factory-admission restriction. Keep README.md accurate within 400 lines and put detail in its linked factory page. pytest, Vitest and Jest remain explicitly unsupported, candidate-controlled adapter registration and external plumbing stay disabled, and old plans are neither migrated nor given inferred metadata.

Foundations: D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301 and D-0305; #452's and #513's ratified plans; #484/D-0311's captured execution API; #503/D-0314's native identity contract; #515/D-0316's shared lifecycle; and decisions recorded for the preceding two issues. Changed SPEC bullets cite existing decisions only. The build cannot write decisions/: the merger records the completed adapter execution/attribution decision before #513's integration issue starts. Decision recording and checks unavailable for lack of Docker/network belong under Merger work in review and do not alone require repair; affected real Python and TLAPS suites remain required in CI.
